params.body:
Phase 1, step 5a of `docs/design/sources-before-more-sources.md`. The judging
half follows in abovebeyond-ai/elixir.

`/api/elixir` gains `extra.collection`:

- **per active adapter**, its declaration (`kind`, `expects`, `dependsOn`) and its
  standing: last run, last outcome and reason, last delivery, the streak of
  non-deliveries and when it began;
- **the adapters that are switched off**, with their reasons;
- **the orphans**: rows in `sources` that are switched on while nothing collects
  them.

The same road the credentials and the binaries took: the app says, Elixir
judges. A test pins that no standing carries a severity, a level or an alert.

## The older witness

`adapter_runs` begins on the day it was built, and the adapters that matter died
long before: TikTok on 12 May, Reddit on 19 August. Judged on runs alone they
would all read "no record yet" for another ten days while the signals table has
known the dates all along. So each standing also carries `lastSignalAt`, asked of
the signals table through the adapter's own claims (by id, by pattern, by type).
It cannot say *why* a source went quiet, only when it last spoke, which is the
part the run history is missing.

## Guarded twice

The field has its own catch: a registry that fails to load costs this one field
and not the heartbeat, the disk and the credentials with it. And it is cached for
five minutes, because the server runs on one thread that the engine shares and
this asks the signals table seventeen questions (measured on the box: about
0.15s each).

771 tests pass, 8 new.
params.title: The app says where its adapters stand
